mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% indicates an exceptionally accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A labor market weakness indicated by UNRATE exceeding 5.0% triggers Fed rate cuts, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) signals an imminent economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO falls and UNRATE rises, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising at least 0.25% in the last 3 months), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days due to higher discount rates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% in 3 months, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 850,000 units signals weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 850.0, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous weakness in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a broad-based demand slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST falls and RSAFS falls, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL index above 230 indicates elevated inflation that pressures the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 230, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decelerating labor market indicated by PAYEMS growth below 0.1% over the past 3 months signals potential Fed rate cuts, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS growth < 0.1% in 3 months, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.
